COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
BA 1st No.195 of 2020
Hon 'b le Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.
 (Via video conferencing).
Mr. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Advocate,
for the applicant.
 Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate
General, for the State of Uttarakhand.
The applicant to the present bail
application is shown to be an accused for the
commission of the offences under Sections 376
(2) (i) (n), 376 (3), 328 and 201 of IPC, as well
as under Section 5(k)/(6) and Section 13/14 of
the Protection of Children from Sexual
Offences Act, 2012, which was registered as
Case Crime No.377 of 2019, at Police Station
Gangnahar, Roorkee, District Haridwar.
The case of the prosecution is that the
present applicant is the brother of the first wife
of the complainant i.e. Mamta. After the death
of first wife, Complainant Babu Ram,
solemnized second marriage with Basanti, from
the second marriage, he had two children,
namely, Rajani Verma who is of 12 yrs of age
and a son Priyanshu, one of the children was
the victim. It was complained of that, after the
second marriage, which was solemnized with
Basanti, the incident has chanced on

29.05.2021, when the applicant has physically
exploited the victim, the same as would be
apparent from the FIR, and the contents
narrated, therein, with regards to the alleged
commission of the offences, in fact, from the
facts narrated and the allegations recorded in
the FIR. The applicant enjoyed the relationship
of being a maternal uncle of the victim. The
allegations are that since he had knowledge of a
paramedical courses, he used to administer
medicine to the victim, and thereafter, he had
fouled with the private parts of the victim, and
not even that the allegations is that he had made
videos and taken nude photographs of the
victim, and threatened her that in case, if she
complained of the incident to anyone, which
has chanced, those videos would be made viral.
On the registration of the FIR, on
27.07.2019, the applicant had filed the bail
application before the learned Trial Court,
which was rejected with the specific finding
recorded therein, that the victim was a minor of
12 years of age, which is a fact not even denied
to the contrary and the commission of offence
was also apparent from the statement of the
prosecutrix, which was recorded under Section
164 of the CrPC, which has been appended as
Annexure No.4, to the counter affidavit.
In fact, the prosecutrix, has supported the
prosecution story and the set of allegations,

about the commission of the offence, and lastly,
if the statement is taken into consideration, it
was on 21.06.2019, where it is alleged by the
victim, that she was forcefully undressed by the
maternal uncle i.e. present applicant, and a
physical relationship was established by him,
against her wishes.
The argument of the learned counsel for
the applicant is that the prosecution story
cannot be sustained for the reason being that the
time gap between the date and the time of
registration of the FIR, and the time of conduct
of medical examination, since being five
minutes only, no reliance can be placed on the
same.
At this stage, this Court is apprehensive
to accept this argument, for the reason being
that, on the contrary a second hand argument,
which has been raised by the learned counsel
for the applicant is that the last sexual
intercourse between them took place on
22.07.2019, and he contends that as per the
medical report, which was submitted on
27.07.2019, non presence of the spermatozoa,
itself would suffice to establish of non
commission of the offences by the applicant.
As far as, the said argument is concerned,
this Court is not willing to accept it, for the
reason being that the last incident complaint of,
is admittedly that of 22.07.2019, the medical

examination was conducted on 27.07.2019, on
the prosecutrix and presence of the spermatozoa
biologically, it is not possible because
obviously in between the intervening period
from 22.07.2019 to 27.07.2019, the victim must
have taken a bath and must have attended the
nature call, where the presence of the
spermatozoa would not be possible. Even
otherwise also, if the medical report itself is
seen, it has reported the prosecutrix she is a girl
of 12 years of age and her hymen is shown to be
torn, as per medical report.
Hence prima facie as per the set of
allegations is concerned, and particularly, the
relationship which the present applicant
enjoyed of being the maternal uncle, the
offence is of very serious in nature, which was
committed on number of occasion with a minor
girl of 12 years, which stands corroborated with
the statement of the victim which was recorded
under Section 164 of the CrPC, as well as the
medical report. Hence, this Court is not inclined
to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application as well
as the short term bail application is rejected.

( Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.)
 17.06.2021
